title: Acyclic hypercover comparison represents the derived section pullback
statement:
Let $h:X'\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with small pro-etale sites and compatible universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ and $R'$ be sheaves of commutative rings on these sites and fix a ring isomorphism $h^{-1}R\cong R'$; use the resulting exact module inverse image $h^*$ and its right adjoint $h_*$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Let $U_\bullet\to X$ and $V_\bullet\to X'$ be augmented simplicial objects of their respective small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Assume that in every degree the map to the finite matching object (the limit of the compatible proper faces, with matching object $X$ or $X'$ in degree zero) is a covering, and that every $U_n$ and $V_n$ is weakly contractible, meaning evaluation of set sheaves there sends epimorphisms to surjections [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible]. Suppose given maps $g_n:V_n\to U_n$ over $h$, commuting with all faces, degeneracies and augmentations. Let $M$ be an $R$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Form nonnegative cochain complexes of abelian groups
$$C_U(M)^n=\Gamma(U_n,M|_{U_n}),\qquad C_V(h^*M)^n=\Gamma(V_n,(h^*M)|_{V_n})$$
with differential $\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^i d_i^*$. The restriction maps induced by $g_n$, using the canonical identification $g_n^*(M|_{U_n})\cong(h^*M)|_{V_n}$, give a cochain map $c_g:C_U(M)\to C_V(h^*M)$. Choose quasi-isomorphisms $M[0]\to I^\bullet$ and $h^*M[0]\to J^\bullet$ into bounded-below complexes of injective module sheaves. Let $T_U,T_V$ be the signed section totals of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-hypercover-total], so that $C_U(M)=T_U(M[0])$ and $C_V(h^*M)=T_V(h^*M[0])$ after forgetting scalars, and let $\alpha_I:I^\bullet(X)\to T_U(I^\bullet)$ and $\alpha_J:J^\bullet(X')\to T_V(J^\bullet)$ be the restriction augmentations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-hypercover-augmentation]. Then the four chain maps $C_U(M)\to T_U(I^\bullet)$, $\alpha_I$, $C_V(h^*M)\to T_V(J^\bullet)$ and $\alpha_J$ are quasi-isomorphisms; the resulting zigzags define the augmentation-normalized comparisons $R\Gamma(X,M[0])\cong C_U(M)$ and $R\Gamma(X',h^*M[0])\cong C_V(h^*M)$ in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], independent of the chosen resolutions. Under these comparisons $c_g$ is identified with the canonical map
$$R\Gamma(X,M[0])\longrightarrow R\Gamma(X',h^*M[0])$$
induced by the actual derived adjunction unit $M[0]\to Rh_*h^*M[0]$ and the canonical composition comparison for derived sections. This identification is natural in $M$, commutes with refinements of both augmented hypercovers, and commutes with composition of such diagrams. No cartesian condition on the squares involving $g_n$ is required; no claim that $c_g$ is a quasi-isomorphism is made.

source.place: Tag 09A2, label lemma-compute-cohomology, injective-resolution proof and restriction augmentations; agent-formulated functoriality refinement for module coefficients and maps over a scheme morphism.

proof.text: Write $i:M[0]\to I$ and $j:h^*M[0]\to J$ for the specified resolutions. Use the total and augmentation definitions to work throughout with differential $\delta+(-1)^p d$. For each coefficient chain map, the section maps commute with both differentials. For a map over $h$, restriction commutes with every face by the assumed simplicial identities and with the coefficient differential by naturality. Consequently the componentwise maps give chain maps on the finite diagonals. The augmentations are the restrictions into bidegree $(0,q)$; their horizontal differential is zero because both faces to degree zero have the same augmentation. In particular the maps in the statement are the actual chain maps, with $T_U(M[0])=C_U(M)$ and $T_V(h^*M[0])=C_V(h^*M)$.

source.place: Tag 09A2, lemma-compute-cohomology; explicit restriction maps and signs

proof.text: Evaluation on each $U_p$ and $V_p$ is exact on module sheaves, including nonaffine weakly contractible objects. Indeed the module forgetful functor is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]; its sheafification hypothesis holds on the small-site presentations of [det-pe-topos-functoriality-site]. A module epimorphism is therefore an abelian-sheaf epimorphism, hence locally surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective], and its underlying set-sheaf map is epi by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective]. Evaluation on a weakly contractible object makes this map surjective by [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible]. Kernels are sectionwise. This proves exactness. Applying evaluation to the short exact sequences defining boundaries, cycles and their quotient identifies the cohomology of the evaluated complex with the evaluation of its cohomology. Thus it carries coefficient quasi-isomorphisms to column quasi-isomorphisms.

The covering precoverage and subcanonicity required for the injective-row theorem hold by [det-pe-topos-functoriality-site]. Given a compatible matching family over a test object, its map into the finite matching object pulls the assumed matching covering back to a covering where the family lifts; in degree zero pull back $U_0\to X$ (respectively $V_0\to X'$). This verifies the local matching hypothesis of [lem-sc-ringed-hypercover-injective-augmentation-ring]. Applying it to every injective module $I^q$ gives exact rows $0\to I^q(X)\to I^q(U_0)\to I^q(U_1)\to\cdots$, and likewise for $J^q$. Choose a common strict lower bound $N$ for $I,J,M[0],h^*M[0]$. The bicomplexes vanish for $p<0$ or $q<N$; the augmentations land in column zero and are killed by the outgoing horizontal differential. The row-augmentation theorem [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-row-augmentation] in abelian groups therefore proves that the specified $\alpha_I$ and $\alpha_J$ are quasi-isomorphisms. No injectivity of the underlying abelian sheaf is used.

source.place: Tag 09A2, final paragraph; hypercovering.tex Tags 01GE/01GW; homology.tex Tag 0133

proof.text: By step 2, evaluation of $i$ or $j$ at any hypercover term is a quasi-isomorphism. The corresponding bicomplex maps have common bounds $p\geq0,q\geq N$. The column-comparison theorem [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-total-column-comparison] proves that $T_U(i)$ and $T_V(j)$ are quasi-isomorphisms. The same argument applies to every quasi-isomorphism between strictly bounded-below coefficient complexes, using the minimum of their lower bounds. All diagonals are finite. Set $A_U^I=T_U(i)^{-1}\alpha_I$ and $A_V^J=T_V(j)^{-1}\alpha_J$ in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. Under the resolution computations of derived sections these are the two claimed comparison isomorphisms.

The given bounded-below injective complexes are K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. Derived functors and their resolution identifications are as in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]; existence on the small ringed sites follows from [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. For two resolutions $i:M[0]\to I$ and $i':M[0]\to I'$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives a comparison $k:I\to I'$, unique up to homotopy, with $ki\simeq i'$. By [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation], $\Gamma(k)$ is exactly the canonical transition between the derived-section models. The augmentation square commutes strictly. Moreover $T_U$ carries a coefficient homotopy $s$ to the homotopy with component $(-1)^p s$ on bidegree $(p,q)$: the horizontal mixed terms cancel, and the vertical terms sum to $ds+sd$. Hence $T_U(k)T_U(i)=T_U(i')$ in the derived category, and cancellation gives $A_U^{I'}\Gamma(k)=A_U^I$. For a coefficient map use the same Hom bijection to lift it between resolutions and the identical calculation. Thus the comparisons are independent of resolutions and natural in coefficients. This argument also applies to $V$.

Since $h^*$ is exact, $h^*i$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The K-injective Hom bijection supplies a chain map $b:h^*I\to J$, unique up to homotopy, with $b\,h^*i\simeq j$. Let $a:I\to h_*J$ be its ordinary chain-adjunction transpose, namely $h_*b\circ\eta_I$. The complex $h_*J$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. Apply the representative formula of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] with left functor $h^*$, right functor $h_*$, right-hand resolution $j$, and identity left resolution (the left functor is exact). It says that the derived transpose of the identity of $h^*M[0]$ is represented by $M[0]\xrightarrow{\eta}h_*h^*M[0]\xrightarrow{h_*j}h_*J$. Naturality of the ordinary unit and $b\,h^*i\simeq j$ give $ai\simeq h_*j\circ\eta_{M[0]}$. Thus $Qa\circ(Qi)^{-1}$ is precisely the actual derived adjunction unit, under the resolution identification $Rh_*h^*M[0]\cong Qh_*J$. This fixes the normalization, rather than choosing an adjunction on isomorphic functors.

source.place: derived.tex Tags 0DVC/09T5, fraction formula for the derived Hom bijection

proof.text: Define $G:T_U(I)\to T_V(J)$ on the $(p,q)$ summand by restriction along $g_p$ followed by $b^q$. Naturality gives $G T_U(i)=T_V(j)c_g$ in the derived category: the coefficient homotopy $b h^*i\simeq j$ induces the signed total homotopy of step 5. There is also the strict equality $G\alpha_I=\alpha_J\Gamma(a)$, where $\Gamma(X,h_*J)=\Gamma(X',J)$: on column zero both sides restrict a global section of $I$ along $V_0\to X'\to X$, then apply $b$, and all other columns are zero. For the ringed-topos morphism $h$ followed by the global-sections morphism to the one-point topos with ring $\mathbf Z$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] identifies the composition comparison with the identity on this section model, because $h_*J$ is already K-injective (take its identity resolution in that theorem). By [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation] and step 6, $\Gamma(a)$ therefore represents the unit-induced derived pullback followed by the canonical composition comparison. Cancelling the four isomorphisms in the two squares yields $c_g A_U^I=A_V^J\Gamma(a)$, the required equality in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$.

source.place: Tag 09A2, restriction augmentation squares; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6E

proof.text: For a refinement $r:U'_\bullet\to U_\bullet$ over the identity, restriction on each $(p,q)$ summand gives a chain map $r_E:T_U(E)\to T_{U'}(E)$, with $r_I\alpha_I=\alpha'_I$ and $r_I T_U(i)=T_{U'}(i)r_M$ strictly. Cancelling gives $r_M A_U=A_{U'}$. The same holds on $V$; the two refinement squares for $c_g$ commute componentwise whenever the diagrams of augmented simplicial maps commute. For a coefficient morphism $M\to L$, restriction and its inverse-image morphism commute on every section, so the square for $c_g$ commutes strictly; combine with step 5 for derived naturality. For consecutive maps $h:X'\to X$ and $k:X''\to X'$ and consecutive augmented simplicial maps, the coefficient identifications $(hk)^*M\cong k^*h^*M$ identify their degree-$p$ section restrictions with the restriction along the composite. Thus $c_{g'}c_g=c_{gg'}$ under these identifications, and cancellation of the common intermediate comparison gives the same equality for the derived-unit maps identified in step 7. Identity maps give identity restrictions. None of these componentwise identities uses a cartesian square, and the proof only inverts the four resolution and augmentation maps, never $c_g$.

Steps 2-4 are the source's two spectral-sequence arguments in bicomplex form. Step 2: exactness of evaluation comes from forgetful exactness, then epi implies locally surjective implies epi of set sheaves, then the weakly-contractible definition; this avoids the affine-only det-pe-wc-sections-exact. Step 3: hypotheses of lem-sc-ringed-hypercover-injective-augmentation-ring verified (precoverage, subcanonicity and smallness from det-pe-topos-functoriality-site; local matching by pulling back the covering U_n→M_n), then the row-augmentation lemma with K^{p,q}=I^q(U_p). Step 4: column comparison with bounds P=0, Q=N. Step 5: recomputed the signed total homotopy (-1)^p s; the mixed δ terms cancel and give ds+sd; independence and naturality follow by cancellation. Step 6: 0DVC formula with s=j, t=id and f=h_*j∘η, whose transpose is j; together with a·i≃h_*j·η this gives the actual derived unit. Step 7: G·α_I=α_J·Γ(a) checked to hold strictly; 0D6E composition applies with the morphism to (pt,Z) and the identity resolution of the K-injective h_*J; cancellation gives c_g·A_U=A_V·Γ(a) in the stated direction. Step 8 (refinement, coefficient and composition compatibility) is elementary given steps 5 and 7. No new nodes, no cycle (closure of 265 nodes), no SGA, no re-split note, statement unchanged. det-pe-hypercover-complex and lem-weil-pbc-proetale-hypercover-computes-bounded-complex give only an unnormalized single-site isomorphism, so they are not duplicates. Edge cases checked: zero sheaf, empty base, constant hypercover, and two points mapping to one point (c_g is not a quasi-isomorphism there, consistent with the statement). The 18 declared tool_uses are generic homological or site tools and are accepted. No changes.

lean.statement: theorem pullback_normalization (U : SimplicialObject (Over (⊤_ X.ProEt))) (V : SimplicialObject (Over (⊤_ Y.ProEt))) (hU : ∀ (n : ℕ) (T : Over (⊤_ X.ProEt)) (μ : U _⦋n⦌ ⟶ T), SimplicialObject.IsProperFaceMatchingArrow U n T μ → Sieve.generate (Presieve.singleton μ.left) ∈ ProEt.topology X T.left) (wU : ∀ n : ℕ, (ProEt.topology X).IsWeaklyContractible.{u + 1} (U _⦋n⦌).left) (hV : ∀ (n : ℕ) (T : Over (⊤_ Y.ProEt)) (μ : V _⦋n⦌ ⟶ T), SimplicialObject.IsProperFaceMatchingArrow V n T μ → Sieve.generate (Presieve.singleton μ.left) ∈ ProEt.topology Y T.left) (wV : ∀ n : ℕ, (ProEt.topology Y).IsWeaklyContractible.{u + 1} (V _⦋n⦌).left) (g : V ⋙ Over.forget (⊤_ Y.ProEt) ⟶ U ⋙ Over.forget (⊤_ X.ProEt) ⋙ proEtaleBaseChange h) (M : proEtaleRingModules X R) : (comparison X R U hU wU).hom.app M ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (restriction h R S c _ _ U V g M) = derivedSectionPullback h R S c M ≫ (comparison Y S V hV wV).hom.app ((proEtaleRingModulePullback h R S c).obj M)
